title: A Cubic Gate-Opening Law for Wide Binaries: a Zero-Parameter Prediction in the Separation Window Current Analyses Exclude
description: Wide binaries at a few kAU probe the weak-field force law below the MOND acceleration scale a0 in systems containing negligible dark matter under any model, so a collisionless-halo picture has essentially no free parameter with which to respond. Published Gaia analyses nonetheless disagree: Chae (2023-2025) reports a boost, Banik, Pittordis & Sutherland (2024) a Newtonian null, and the two differ by delta gamma_v ~ 0.174 -- about 2.1x the entire boost predicted by a de Sitter-Unruh MODIFIED-INERTIA framework with a0 = cH_Lambda/Z, Z = sqrt(32pi/3) = 5.78881, a0 = 9.36e-11 m/s^2. An amplitude test cannot survive that spread. We point out that the same framework, when its committed low-pass response gate G(omega) = 1/(1 + i omega/omega_c) with omega_c in [1.782, 2.211]e-14 rad/s is applied to the ORBITAL frequency of the pair, makes a much sharper prediction along a SHAPE axis that has never been examined. A binary's orbital frequency Omega = sqrt(GM/s^3) exceeds omega_c throughout the analysed separation range, so the gate is shut and the framework predicts a NEWTONIAN result at 2-30 kAU. Because Omega falls as s^(-3/2), the gate does not open at a threshold but as Re G -> (omega_c^2/GM) s^3, giving gamma_v(s) - 1 = (1/2)[nu(y_ext) - 1](omega_c^2/GM) s^3, with the exponent equal to 3 BY DERIVATION rather than by fit (measured local slope 3.00 at 5 kAU, falling to 0.06 once saturated) and the amplitude fixed entirely by omega_c, the measured pair mass, and the measured Galactic external field. There are no free parameters and the exponent is not adjustable. Three distinct mass powers follow from the same closed form and are recovered numerically over 0.5-5.0 Msun: the knee radius r_gate = (GM/omega_c^2)^(1/3) ~ M^0.3333, the external-field plateau radius r_efe = sqrt(GM/g_ext) ~ M^0.5000, and the fixed-separation excess ~ M^(-0.9935) (asymptotic; knee-contaminated to M^(-0.857) by 30 kAU, and both values are reported). Every published contaminant channel -- chance alignment, unresolved tertiaries, close-binary contamination -- carries a fixed velocity scale and therefore rises as s^(1/2): exponent 0.5 against 3.0, so signal and contamination have DIFFERENT separation dependences and a joint fit is well posed in principle. The observational consequence is the point of this note: gamma_v rises from 1.0125 at 30 kAU, the cut adopted by every published analysis, to 1.0932 at 200 kAU, within the reach of the public El-Badry, Rix & Heintz (2021, MNRAS 506, 2269) Gaia DR3 catalogue -- a factor of 7 in excess, across a window excluded by a cut chosen to control chance-alignment contamination, for reasons unrelated to this prediction. At the 30 kAU cut the predicted excess (1.2e-2) lies an order of magnitude below the inter-group systematic, so the conventional window CANNOT test the framework; that is itself the result. The gate does not damage the galactic case, which is the check that makes the gated branch admissible: across the Milky Way solar circle and outer disk, dwarfs, low-surface-brightness disks, massive spirals and the inner disk, the largest value found is Omega/omega_c = 0.364 (Re G >= 0.883), so the gate is open in galaxies and shut in wide binaries -- the radial acceleration relation and the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation are untouched, and wide binaries become a DIFFERENT REGIME rather than the same physics at smaller scale. COSTS ARE STATED IN THE ABSTRACT, NOT BURIED. (i) The result is CONDITIONAL on an unresolved question about the framework's own kernel: whether K(Box_u) responds to the acceleration MAGNITUDE |a|, which is constant on a circular orbit and would leave the gate open (recovering the ungated gamma_v ~ 1.09), or acts as the linear operator its covariant form suggests, selecting the gated branch computed here. A linear kernel cannot sense |a| = sqrt(a^mu a_mu), which is not a linear functional of the trajectory, and the framework's own field-theory analysis reduces the matter-sector kernel to K(-q0^2), a function of the FREQUENCY q0 alone -- both point to the gated branch, but neither closes it. On the ungated branch this note is VOID. The branches lie 4.9-5.8 sigma apart in the framework's own DR4 error model and the choice must be frozen before Gaia DR4 or the test is post hoc; the same fork governs the framework's apparent Gdot/G floor, since the lunar mean motion exceeds omega_c by ~1.5e8. (ii) A DEEPER prior question is not addressed: if the kernel is a function of frequency (or, in the eikonal limit, of momentum) rather than of acceleration, whether the construction reproduces an acceleration-dependent inertia law AT ALL is open; this note assumes the MI law as given and is not evidence on that question. (iii) FEASIBILITY beyond 50 kAU is unresolved and may be fatal to a DR3 test, since contamination also grows with separation and whether signal-to-contamination IMPROVES cannot be settled without the catalogue in hand. (iv) A confirmed s^3 rise would establish a FREQUENCY scale omega_c, NOT the coefficient Z: Z = 5.7888 and the conventional 2pi = 6.2832 differ by only 7.87%, both lie inside the +/-16% empirical a0 box, and no arena examined here separates them -- and, against interest, matching Chae (2024b)'s central gamma on this framework's own kernel would require a0 ~ 1.9x canonical, which at face value disfavours the Lambda-tied coefficient specifically. (v) Nothing here bears on whether dark matter exists: a wide-binary result constrains the weak-field FORCE LAW, not the matter content, and gamma_v = 1 is Newton's prediction, shared by LambdaCDM, by this framework's own gated branch, and by hybrid modified-force-plus-particle models. CREDIT: the kernel nu(y) = sqrt(1+1/y) and the excess identity g_obs^2 - g_bar^2 = a0 g_bar ARE Milgrom (1999, Phys. Lett. A 253, 273) Eqs. (8)-(9), with coefficient 2cH_Lambda -- a ratio of exactly 2Z to the value used here -- and Milgrom (1999, 2015) and Smolin (2017, Phys. Rev. D 96, 083523) had already tied a0 to Lambda with a 2pi coefficient. Priority for tying a0 to Lambda is explicitly NOT claimed and cannot be, since Z and 2pi differ by 7.87%. The distinctive content is the coefficient cH_Lambda/Z together with a covariant modified-inertia completion, plus the prediction reported here. Four independent falsification conditions are given. omega_c is anchored by no independent theoretical argument (a dimensional census places every intrinsic scale 3.2-5.6 decades away) and is the framework's most exposed quantity. a0's value, Z, the response sign, and omega_c remain POSTULATED, never asserted to be derived. Both a0 footings (cH_Lambda/Z and cH0/Z, differing by ~21%) and both omega_c window edges are carried through every number. All quantitative claims are reproduced by two committed Python scripts, both exit 0 with no hard-coded verdicts, at https://github.com/carlzimmerman/zimmerman-formula (real_research/reviews/mi_wb_gate_fork_2026.py, 11/11 checks; real_research/reviews/mi_wb_cubic_rise_2026.py, 10/10 checks). Two assertions failed their own checks on first run and were corrected in place rather than patched, and the corrections are recorded in the paper and the commit history. This is a conditional prediction paper, not a discovery paper and not a claim of a theory of everything.
notes: Conditional prediction paper. Derives an s^3 gate-opening law for wide binaries from the framework's committed omega_c response gate applied to the orbital frequency, with the exponent derived rather than fitted and zero free parameters in the amplitude. Central observational claim: the entire predicted signal lies beyond the ~30 kAU cut used by every published wide-binary analysis, within the reach of the public El-Badry, Rix & Heintz (2021) catalogue. Strict both-ways discipline maintained: the gated branch is favoured by two independent structural arguments but is NOT closed, and the paper states in its abstract that on the alternative branch the entire result is VOID. Feasibility beyond 50 kAU is flagged as unresolved and possibly fatal to a DR3 test. Quarantine held throughout (a0, Z, response sign, omega_c never asserted derived); both a0 footings and both omega_c edges carried on every number. Milgrom (1999) credited in the abstract and Section 1 for the kernel and the identity; priority for the a0-Lambda tie explicitly disclaimed. Publish as a NEW record. Companion to the framework record DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20721540. Reproducible from https://github.com/carlzimmerman/zimmerman-formula.
